meta.note: Documentation fields and v7 operational constraints are deliberately separated; earlier casing examples are not final v7 authority.

principles.title: Be Concise and Eliminate Unnecessary Words
principles.v7Title: Be Concise and Eliminate Unnecessary Words
principles.description: Mobile screens are small. Every word must earn its place by helping users complete tasks.
principles.technique: Remove filler words, combine ideas, use active voice

principles.title: Use Clear, Simple, and Jargon-Free Language
principles.v7Title: Use Clear, Simple, and Jargon-Free Language
principles.description: Avoid acronyms, banking jargon, and complex sentences. Plain language builds trust.
principles.technique: Replace technical terms with user-friendly equivalents

principles.title: Maintain a Conversational, Human Tone
principles.description: Write like talking to a user in person — friendly, warm, professional. Not robotic, not overly casual.
principles.technique: Use contractions, second person ('you'), active voice

principles.title: Provide Context and Helpful Guidance
principles.description: Users should understand what to do and why. Explain both the task and its purpose.
principles.technique: Title states WHAT; body explains WHY or provides helpful detail

principles.title: Use Specific and Predictable CTAs and an Action-Oriented Language
principles.description: Users should instantly know what tapping a button will do. Specific verbs build trust.
principles.technique: Start with action verb, be specific about outcome

principles.title: Be Empathetic, Optimistic, Use Positive Wording to Create Good Feelings
principles.v7Title: Be Empathetic and Use Positive Framing
principles.description: Reduce anxiety with supportive language. Celebrate progress, acknowledge effort, avoid blame.
principles.technique: Focus on what IS possible, not what ISN'T; celebrate milestones

principles.title: Optimize for Mobile-Specific Interactions
principles.description: Consider touch, swipe, and small screens. Use mobile-appropriate language.
principles.technique: Use 'tap' not 'click'; design for thumb reach; keep scannable

principles.title: Write Inclusive Microcopy
principles.description: Avoid idioms, cultural references, and gendered language that might exclude users.
principles.technique: Gender-neutral pronouns; avoid idioms; test for cultural appropriateness

principles.title: Write Clear and Reassuring Success Messages
principles.v7Title: Write Clear and Reassuring Success Messages
principles.description: Confirm actions with key details. User should feel confident the action completed.
principles.technique: State what happened + key details (amount, destination, timing)

principles.title: Write Helpful Error Messages and Failure scenarios
principles.description: Explain what went wrong, why if known, how to fix, and reassure about money/data.

documentation.useCase: Loan Application, Repayment, Wallet Top-up
principles: Use Clear, Simple, and Jargon-Free Language
Use Specific and Predictable CTAs and an Action-Oriented Language
Optimize for Mobile-Specific Interactions
documentation.rationale: Primary buttons must guide users confidently. Weak verbs or abstract labels increase hesitation, especially during financial actions.

rules.use_case: Primary actions: Loan Application, Payments, Wallet Top-up, Form Submission, Onboarding Entry
transformation_rules: Start with a strong action verb
Be specific about what happens when tapped
For onboarding entry points, prefer 'Start' over 'Continue'
For authentication, prefer 'Get OTP' over 'Send OTP' (user-centric framing)
For submissions, prefer 'Confirm [X]' over generic 'Submit'

patternGuidance.mental_model: User taps this to DO something specific — label must tell them exactly what will happen
patternGuidance.length_target: 2-3 words optimal; 1 word acceptable for universal actions

documentation.useCase: Optional navigation, alternative actions
principles: Use Clear, Simple, and Jargon-Free Language
Use Specific and Predictable CTAs and an Action-Oriented Language
Optimize for Mobile-Specific Interactions
documentation.rationale: Secondary buttons are helpful alternatives. Copy must feel optional yet actionable.

rules.use_case: Alternative actions, dismissals, deferrals, secondary paths
transformation_rules: Provide clear alternative to primary action
For deferrals, use softer phrasing: 'Maybe Later' over 'Remind me later'
Maintain symmetry with primary button where logical

documentation.useCase: Less prominent or optional actions
principles: Be Concise and Eliminate Unnecessary Words
Use Specific and Predictable CTAs and an Action-Oriented Language
Optimize for Mobile-Specific Interactions
documentation.rationale: Tertiary buttons support optional paths. Copy should not distract from primary actions.

rules.use_case: Less prominent actions, navigation helpers, 'see more' patterns

documentation.useCase: List item actions, Selections
principles: Use Clear, Simple, and Jargon-Free Language
Use Specific and Predictable CTAs and an Action-Oriented Language
Optimize for Mobile-Specific Interactions
documentation.rationale: List buttons route users to next steps. They must feel intuitive and informative.

rules.use_case: Actionable list items, navigation links, feature access points

identification.description: List items that function as CTAs — identified by action affordances

transformation_rules: Always use at least 2 words — single words are too vague
Be specific about destination or action
Add 'Your' for personalisation where appropriate

documentation.useCase: Transactions,, FAQs, Permissions, Navigation Links
documentation.phrasing: Phrases for most items; full sentences for guidance
principles: Be Concise and Eliminate Unnecessary Words
Use Clear, Simple, and Jargon-Free Language
Optimize for Mobile-Specific Interactions
documentation.goodExamples:
- "Pay with UPI ID"
- "Add Bank Account"
- "We use facial data..."
documentation.rationale: Lists must be easy to scan and understand, guiding users through actions or info with minimal friction.

rules.use_case: Informational list items, non-actionable display rows, static content lists

identification.description: List items that display information only — no action affordances
identification.distinguish_from: List Button — if item has action affordances, use List Button instead

transformation_rules: Title conveys the primary information
Body provides supporting context if needed
Do not phrase as actions — these are not tappable

documentation.useCase: Terminal States: Error Messages, Processing, Success, Instructional Prompts
documentation.tone:
Title: Instructional, 
 Prompting to take action
Body: Descriptive, Empathetic, Supportive
principles: Use Clear, Simple, and Jargon-Free Language
Maintain a Conversational, Human Tone
Provide Context and Helpful Guidance
Be Empathetic, Optimistic, Use Positive Wording to Create Good Feelings
Write Inclusive Microcopy
documentation.goodExamples:
Header: "Details could not be verified"
Body: "Try again with a different ID"

Header: Enter your PAN
Body: PAN is a regulatory requirement by RBI for KYC.

Header: Share your email ID
Body: Email helps recover your account in case you forget your password
documentation.rationale:
Text blocks support users in high-stakes moments. Copy must reassure, explain, and instruct clearly. 

Title and Primary CTA should have a common word which creates association of prompt and action on any screen.

rules.use_case: Terminal states (success, error, processing), instructional prompts, screen headers

structure_pattern.title: Action phrase or state declaration
structure_pattern.body: Context, explanation, or next step guidance

transformation_rules: Title tells WHAT; body tells WHY or HOW
For instructions: title = action to take, body = reason or context
For errors: title = what went wrong, body = how to fix
For success: title = what happened, body = what's next
Add 'Your' to titles for personalisation: 'Enter Your Email' not 'Enter Email'

documentation.useCase:
Communication messages or user prompts in a bottom sheet modal.
Provides instructions, status updates,  exit friction, or guidance during key user journeys (e.g., loan application, verification, payment).
documentation.tone:
Title: Instructional, 
 Promting to take action
principles: Be Concise and Eliminate Unnecessary Words
Use Clear, Simple, and Jargon-Free Language
Maintain a Conversational, Human Tone
Provide Context and Helpful Guidance
Optimize for Mobile-Specific Interactions
documentation.goodExamples:
Title: “We couldn’t verify your ID”
Body: “Upload a valid government ID to continue your loan application.”

Title: “Loan approved!”
Body: “Your funds will be deposited shortly. Check your wallet for details.”
documentation.badExamples:
“Oops!” (vague titles with no context).

Titles in ALL CAPS or with unnecessary exclamation marks.

Overly casual or joking language in serious contexts.
documentation.rationale:
Used for communication messages or user prompts in the Branch App—delivering instructions, state updates, or guidance during key flows (e.g., loan application, verification, payment).
Variants: title-only, title + body, optional icon (for terminal states).

rules.use_case: Modal prompts, confirmations, exit friction, contextual guidance
transformation_rules: Title must be understandable without reading body
For confirmations, use question format: 'Are You Sure...?'
For success states, be celebratory but brief
Keep body concise — users want to act, not read

documentation.useCase: Action Confirmation, Status Update, Error Notification
principles: Use Clear, Simple, and Jargon-Free Language
Be Empathetic, Optimistic, Use Positive Wording to Create Good Feelings
Write Clear and Reassuring Success Messages
Write Helpful Error Messages and Failure scenarios
documentation.rationale: Toasts give real-time feedback with minimal interruption. Copy must be brief, relevant, and emotionally aligned.

rules.use_case: Action confirmations, status updates, brief notifications
transformation_rules: NEVER use exclamation marks — they feel shouty
NEVER use terminal punctuation for fragment-style toasts
State what happened in past tense: 'Profile updated' not 'Profile has been updated!'
Be specific: 'Bank account added' not 'Added successfully'
Remove words like 'successfully' when the positive outcome is obvious

documentation.useCase: Critical Notifications, Warnings, Payment Reminders
documentation.tone:
Urgent but respectful, 
Clear and action-oriented
principles: Use Clear, Simple, and Jargon-Free Language
Be Empathetic, Optimistic, Use Positive Wording to Create Good Feelings
Write Helpful Error Messages and Failure scenarios
documentation.goodExamples:
- "Loan repayment due"
- "Your loan of Ksh 20,000 is overdue. Pay now to avoid penalty"
- CTA: "Pay Now"
documentation.rationale: Alerts inform users of urgent or sensitive updates. Tone should guide without alarming.

rules.use_case: Critical notifications, warnings, payment reminders, blocking errors
transformation_rules: Title should convey urgency level without alarming
Message must include actionable next step
For money-related alerts, always reassure about funds safety
CTA should be specific: 'Pay now' not 'OK'

documentation.category:
Small Banner: Actionable
Large Banner: Informational
documentation.useCase:
Small Banner: Credit Score Prompts, Loan Offers, Investment Promos, Bill Pay Rewards, 
Large Banner: Spash Screens
principles: Use Clear, Simple, and Jargon-Free Language
Provide Context and Helpful Guidance
Be Empathetic, Optimistic, Use Positive Wording to Create Good Feelings
Write Helpful Error Messages and Failure scenarios
documentation.goodExamples:
- "Earn more than a fixed deposit with Branch Invest"
- "Get your Credit Score for free"
- CTA: "Start Investing", "Apply Now", "Download Now"
documentation.badExamples:
- "Click here to view offer" -
- "You won’t believe what you get"
documentation.rationale: Banners communicate key benefits quickly. Copy must focus on clarity, confidence, and visual alignment.

rules.use_case: Promotional content, feature highlights, credit score prompts, offers
transformation_rules: Lead with user benefit, not product feature
Avoid hype words: 'amazing', 'incredible', 'best ever'
Be specific about numbers: 'up to 13% returns' not 'great returns'
Never make guarantees about financial outcomes

documentation.useCase: Nested Inside outline cards to display Loan Balances, Wallet Amounts, Card Summaries
documentation.phrasing: Static data label- data value pairs
principles: Be Concise and Eliminate Unnecessary Words
Use Clear, Simple, and Jargon-Free Language
Provide Context and Helpful Guidance
Write Clear and Reassuring Success Messages
documentation.rationale: Data Display elements provide critical figures clearly, making numbers scannable and contextually relevant.

rules.use_case: Displaying loan balances, account details, transaction info, user data
transformation_rules: Spell out abbreviations: 'Account Number' not 'Acc No.'
No colons after labels
Remove leading zeros from numeric values: '6' not '06'
Use proper currency formatting with thousands separators

documentation.useCase: Forms, Search, Inline Chat Input, PIN Code input, Star Input, Dropdowns
documentation.phrasing: Labels: Noun phrases, Hints: Instructional, Errors: Sentences
principles: Be Concise and Eliminate Unnecessary Words
Use Clear, Simple, and Jargon-Free Language
Provide Context and Helpful Guidance
Write Inclusive Microcopy
documentation.rationale: Text fields guide entry and provide feedback. Copy must be clear and constructive across all states.

rules.use_case: Form fields, search boxes, PIN entry, dropdowns
rules.structure_pattern: Noun phrase describing what to enter
transformation_rules: Use 'Select' not 'Choose' for dropdowns
Add 'your' for personalisation in instructional contexts
Market-specific terminology applies (see markets.json)

documentation.useCase: Forms, Search, Inline Chat Input, PIN Code input, Star Input, Dropdowns
principles: Use Clear, Simple, and Jargon-Free Language
Provide Context and Helpful Guidance
Be Empathetic, Optimistic, Use Positive Wording to Create Good Feelings
documentation.goodExamples:
- "Charges may be applied by your bank"
- "Name should be as per you PAN"
- "It is advised to add your bank account linked with UPI"
documentation.rationale: Hints guides users in better decision making and reduce errors. In some cases, we guide users to provide specific details we need.

rules.use_case: Helper text below inputs, validation error messages
transformation_rules: Hints explain WHY, not just WHAT
Errors: state problem + solution, never blame user
Use 'you entered' to personalise errors
For format errors, show example

documentation.useCase: Forms, Search, Inline Chat Input, PIN Code input, Star Input, Dropdowns
documentation.rationale: Placeholders help users with understanding the type of input or the number of characters in a form field

rules.use_case: Ghost text showing expected format
transformation_rules: Show format, not instruction
For dates, use market format: 'DD MMM YYYY'
Use 'e.g.,' prefix for examples

documentation.useCase: Transaction Details, Loan Summaries, Payment Schedules, EMI Breakdown
principles: Be Concise and Eliminate Unnecessary Words
Use Clear, Simple, and Jargon-Free Language
Provide Context and Helpful Guidance
Write Clear and Reassuring Success Messages
documentation.badExamples:
- "Click here to see more"
- "Loan got disbursed successfully"
documentation.rationale: Tables must support scannability and clarity for dense data. Headers guide orientation, rows reflect user actions.

rules.use_case: Transaction details, payment schedules, loan summaries
transformation_rules: Headers use Title Case for scannability
Cells use sentence case
Use proper date formatting: 'DD MMM YYYY'
Hyphenate compound adjectives: 'On-Time Payments'

documentation.useCase: Loan Repayment schedules, FAQs, breakdowns, multi-step flows
principles: Be Concise and Eliminate Unnecessary Words
Use Clear, Simple, and Jargon-Free Language
Provide Context and Helpful Guidance
documentation.goodExamples: "View Details", "Read More", “Why we need your ID”
documentation.rationale: Accordions help users scan and reveal layered info. Clarity in collapsed and expanded states is essential.

rules.use_case: FAQs, repayment schedules, expandable explanations
transformation_rules: Header should be scannable
Avoid generic headers like 'More details'
Frame as questions where appropriate

documentation.useCase: Filtering Transactions, Filtering Accounts, Category Selection
principles: Be Concise and Eliminate Unnecessary Words
Optimize for Mobile-Specific Interactions
documentation.rationale: Chips should support fast filtering with short, user-friendly labels.

rules.use_case: Filters, category selection, quick toggles
transformation_rules: Keep very short — chips compete for horizontal space
Use consistent naming within a chip group

documentation.useCase: Notifications, Message Counts, Status Indicators
principles: Be Concise and Eliminate Unnecessary Words
Write Clear and Reassuring Success Messages
documentation.rationale: Badges signal urgent or status-related data. Text must be concise and visually scannable.

rules.use_case: Notification counts, status indicators
transformation_rules: Numbers over 99 display as '99+'
Status words: 'New', 'Due', 'Pending'

documentation.useCase: Status Tags, Counts, Notifications
principles: Be Concise and Eliminate Unnecessary Words
Use Clear, Simple, and Jargon-Free Language
Provide Context and Helpful Guidance

rules.use_case: Status tags, category indicators
transformation_rules: Use consistent status vocabulary

documentation.useCase: Multi-step KYC process, onboarding form
principles: Use Clear, Simple, and Jargon-Free Language
Provide Context and Helpful Guidance
Be Empathetic, Optimistic, Use Positive Wording to Create Good Feelings
documentation.goodExamples:
- "Step 1 of 3: Allow permissions" 
- "Step 2 of 5: Upload Documents"
- "Step 3 of 5: Add a bank acount" - "Step 4 of 5: Add income details"
documentation.rationale: Step indicators orient users in long flows. Copy should guide and motivate clearly at each stage.

rules.use_case: Multi-step flows, KYC progress, onboarding
transformation_rules: Use 'Confirm' not 'Verify' for user-initiated confirmations
Be specific about what each step accomplishes

documentation.useCase: App loading, form submission, saving
principles: Provide Context and Helpful Guidance
Be Empathetic, Optimistic, Use Positive Wording to Create Good Feelings

rules.use_case: Loading states, processing indicators

Ellipsis allowed for loading states
